card.name: Table headers and dose-sentence endings
card.fires_on: Fires on the last piece of a word or a sentence-ending period inside dosing and radiation-dose table text. Examples are the end of ABSORBED in table headers and the period after mcg/kg/day.

modes.label: Period after trace-element dose
modes.description: The full stop ending a sentence that gives a per-kg daily dose of copper or selenium.
modes.example: For pediatric patients, the suggested additive dosage level is 20 mcg copper/kg/day<<.>> The normal plasma range for copper is approximately

modes.label: Radiation table header
modes.description: The end of ABSORBED in the column header of organ radiation dose tables.
modes.example: Table 2. Estimated Absorbed Radiation Dose from AdreView ORGAN / TISSUE ABSOR<<BED>> DOSE PER UNIT ADMINISTERED ACT

modes.label: Inside heading phrases
modes.description: Linking or partial pieces within capitalized headings such as fetal ductus or follicular lymphoma terms.
modes.example: Premature Closure<< of>> Fetal Ductus Arterios

card.writes: It seems to suppress odd name-like continuations and lightly promote capitalized technical word starts such as Ox, Cath and Tit.
card.plain: It fires on table headers and sentence ends in dosing sections, where the next word is a new capitalized term.
